mechanics.title: 5 ETH per block
mechanics.text: Miners earn 5 ETH per block, plus uncle rewards. Fees go to the miner.

mechanics.title: 3 ETH per block
mechanics.text: Byzantium cuts the block reward to 3 ETH (EIP-649).

mechanics.title: 2 ETH per block
mechanics.text: Constantinople cuts the block reward to 2 ETH (EIP-1234).

mechanics.title: Fees start to burn
mechanics.text: London burns the base fee of every transaction (EIP-1559). Supply can now shrink when use is high.

mechanics.title: Mining issuance ends
mechanics.text: The Merge removes block rewards. New ETH goes only to validators, and the amount grows with total stake.

mechanics.title: Blob fees burn too
mechanics.text: Dencun adds blob gas. The blob base fee is burned, like the normal base fee (EIP-4844).

mechanics.title: Blob fee floor
mechanics.text: Fusaka ties the minimum blob fee to execution cost (EIP-7918), so cheap blobs still burn some ETH.

narratives.label: Crypto-fuel
narratives.text: The whitepaper calls ether the main internal crypto-fuel of Ethereum: it pays for transactions.

narratives.label: Triple-point asset
narratives.text: Bankless frames ETH as three assets at once: capital (staking), consumable (gas) and store of value.

narratives.label: Ultrasound money
narratives.text: With the EIP-1559 burn, supporters argue ETH can become deflationary, 'better than sound money'.

narratives.label: Security budget
narratives.text: ETH's value pays for the security of the chain: staked ETH is what an attacker must beat.

narratives.label: Store of value
narratives.text: Vitalik says to stop valuing ETH by fee burn. Its value is stability from decentralization, censorship resistance and security.
